# Why tide pools stay warm

Tide pools trap seawater at low tide. The water in a shallow pool heats up in the sun, sometimes by ten degrees in an afternoon.
Small crabs hide under the rocks because the water there stays cooler. A pool that is refreshed by the next high tide cools again.

Marine biologists at the Tinyfield station count the animals in forty pools every spring.
